claims.text: Character::F_ApplyResult 0x3b10b4 dispatches first to attacker CharAI at Character+968, then defender CharAI at the same offset, both virtual slot +180 with the same (attacker, defender, result). Result mask 0x20000000 suppresses both. Online authority can return before this tail.

AISDefault::InitVCB 0x3dc7d8 records 0x800 for OnTargetHit and 0x1000 for OnTargetMissed. OnCombatResults 0x3dc9a8 sends missed when outcome byte+24 has either low bit set; otherwise hit, subject to callback registration.

StealAIEvent is defined in skills/_commons.luac. It installs an AIEventProxy through AddToVFTable and invokes stored listeners while temporarily changing SKILL_ID. It is not a missing native registration named StealAIEvent.

claims.text: The original _F_CalculateResult 0x3b2638 requests Random(100), then shifts the random integer left by 8 before the chance helper. Random uses seed modulo the positive bound, so the comparison domain is integers 0..99 multiplied by 256.

Mode 2 stun and push use resolved SnS chance properties 184 and 183. If the raw chance is positive, the effective threshold is chance + 5*attacker_level_raw - defender_resistance_raw - 5*defender_level_raw; strict threshold > random_raw succeeds. Stun resistance is 138; push resistance is 136.

Values such as 80+5L and 185+4L are chance percentage points represented in fixed256, not an 8-bit probability divided by 256. A base above 100 can still fail after defender resistance and level adjustment. A successful roll is also separate from state admission, including the boss rejection in SM_SetStunState.

SkillCombatRoll(object) is a Lua wrapper passing SKILL_ID to SkillCombatRoll__(SKILL_ID, object), whose registered handler is Character::_SkillCombatRoll 0x3b9fbc; it runs F_SkillAttack and then F_ApplyResult.

claims.text: PROPS_AddBuff 0x3e232c maps capacity<=0 to128. Replacement/reuse scans run only when current count equals requested capacity. Lower unsigned strength entries qualify and their strength is immediately rewritten; equal-strength permanent entries qualify; timed ties compare elapsed time through TMR_TimeLeft. This is not a general FIFO eviction policy.

At full capacity, if no entry qualifies, allocation is refused and nullptr returned. A qualifying entry is reused after stopping its prior timer; nonzero duration starts a one-shot event54 timer, zero duration is permanent. ResetSheet initializes defaults before SnS_Level receives strength<<8.

Combination depends on each property type from AAA_TYPES_DONT_DELETE, not a universal buff-sum rule. Type&4 accumulates; type&2 takes base then saved then gear, then first ascending declaration with a set value (last set instance in that group); type&1 favors the highest descending declaration group, then gear/saved/base. Type&32 uses base+saved; type&16 uses base. Defaults identify unset values.

The native buff kernel and property resolver are recovered, but Windows RuntimeTimedBuffOwnerV1 currently replaces every matching class instance on application and exposes no arbitrary native capacity selection. Its source is a partial production adaptation of the original buff-map contract.

claims.text: Character::_RemoveBuff 0x3b842c calls PROPS_DelBuff on the bound receiver at Character+1376. The optional pointer selects an instance inside that receiver's class declaration; it never changes the receiver to the pointer's owner.

The first argument must be numeric and less than ClassTable size. With one argument deletion uses nullptr; with a second pointer-tag argument the pointer is supplied to PROPS_DelBuff 0x3e101c. Invalid first types/IDs or unsupported second types do not enter deletion.

PROPS_DelBuff removes a sole instance regardless of the supplied pointer; for multiple instances it requires a nonnull exact pointer match. Thus receiverA:RemoveBuff(class, receiverB_handle) can delete A's sole instance, but does not delete B's buff.

claims.text: SM_SetStunState 0x3c5ffc rejects bosses first. It obtains GetCharAnimTableId 0x3a3228 (invalid authored ID falls back to17), then validates the returned row against CharAnimTable size. It reads the Stunned field at byte140 of the160-byte native row, not an arbitrary hardcoded animation.

Only when pending bit2 is absent does it start timer43 for the supplied unsigned integer milliseconds; reapplying while pending does not restart that timer. The timer response is ignored by this source caller, then pending bit2 is set.

It queries AnimStancedAnim.SL__LIST_IPHONE mask0x200. If present, GetAnimStance is added to the base Stunned sequence; otherwise modifier0. The selected sequence is stored at machine+40. Force enters state9 through _SetState; otherwise event50012 is raised. Requested mode adds flag0x800 after that transition/event.

claims.text: Character::createBindings 0x3b56bc explicitly registers ApplyBuff both as global bound function and object method to Character::_ApplyPropClass 0x3babdc. The atlas alias is correct; this is not a guessed similarly named routine.

A numeric class first argument and nonnull pointer second argument select PROPS_ApplyClassToSheet on the bound receiver. That routine invokes _LoadClass(sheet,class,true), then _ApplyPropClass recalculates receiver properties. A boolean second argument selects PROPS_ApplyClass instead; omitted second argument uses the nonbuff false branch.

The source wrapper allows class index equal to size past its `>` gate, but _LoadClass subsequently admits only indices strictly less than size. The supplied pointer is a native sheet; the wrapper does not prove ownership or lifetime beyond its null check.
